source.name: Bengaluru Comprehensive Mobility Plan / Revised Master Plan traffic counts
source.note: Used only to identify documented high-volume junctions and peak-sensitive areas. No zone-specific travel-time multiplier is inferred from these counts.

orr-east.message: This area contains several documented high-volume junctions on the eastern ring-road corridor. Peak periods are especially disruption-sensitive.

whitefield.message: The Whitefield approach includes documented high-volume junctions such as Kundalahalli and Doddanekundi, so commute peaks can deteriorate quickly when anything unusual happens.

south-east.message: Central Silk Board is one of Bengaluru's most heavily loaded documented junctions. Morning and evening commute windows are particularly sensitive.

north-airport.message: Hebbal and nearby northern junctions carry very high documented traffic volumes. Airport and city-bound peaks can become severe when disruptions overlap normal demand.

central.message: The current public junction dataset is not strong enough to create a separate Central Bengaluru peak profile, so the citywide historical pattern is used without a local modifier.

south.message: South Bengaluru includes documented busy junctions such as Sarakki and Devegowda Petrol Bunk. Peak windows can be locally sensitive even when the citywide pattern looks manageable.

west.message: West Bengaluru includes high-volume junctions such as Goragunte Palya and Sumanahalli. Holiday departure and return traffic can also matter on outbound corridors.
